verdict.headline: New tariffs on 99.4% of US imports land on FOMC week with six regime indicators still breached
verdict.label: Step Aside — Trump tariff escalation + Asia rout + Brent $100 = protect capital before July 29 META/MSFT capex verdict
verdict.horizon: Through FOMC July 28-29 and META/MSFT/AMZN earnings July 29-30
verdict.rationale_short: Friday's pre-open is a fragile tentative bounce (+0.2% ES) against a compounding adverse backdrop: Trump's next phase of tariffs — 10-12.5% on 60 countries covering 99.4% of US imports — went into effect this morning, backfilling a blanket tariff the Supreme Court deemed unlawful, simultaneously adding a fresh stagflationary input on top of Brent crude above $100 and a September rate-hike probability of 82%. Asia bore the brunt overnight: Nikkei -2.9%, KOSPI -5% (sidecar circuit-breaker triggered), MSCI Asia Pacific -2.2%. Six of seven regime indicators remain in formal breach. SPX is 28 points from the 7,380 level that converts the regime to formal BEARISH. Intel's Thursday-night blowout — revenue $16.1B vs. $14.4B consensus, EPS $0.42 vs. $0.22 — validated AI demand breadth, but the stock reversed in after-hours trading from the $110 spike, limiting its lifting power for Friday's open. The week ahead is the most consequential of the year: FOMC July 28-29, META and MSFT reporting July 29 after close, Amazon July 30 — all facing the same AI-capex-ROI scrutiny that took Alphabet -7% on Thursday.

trade_setups.thesis: Intel's Q2 results were the most important positive data point of the week: revenue $16.13B (+25% YoY, fastest in 15 years) against a $14.42B consensus; non-GAAP EPS $0.42 nearly doubled the $0.22 estimate; Data Center & AI segment grew 59% YoY; Q3 guided to $16.3B midpoint above consensus. Apple and Microsoft confirmed as 18A foundry partners. The AH reversal from $110 (on the $11B GAAP net loss) was a valuation adjustment, not a fundamental repudiation. This is the clearest validation that enterprise AI demand has broadened beyond the four major hyperscalers into the broader corporate infrastructure cycle.

bear_case: Counter-thesis: The bear case now has three mutually reinforcing legs where before it had two. The oil shock (Brent $100.40, first close above $100 since May 26) and the September rate hike trajectory (82%) were already in place when Thursday closed with SPX 28 points from the formal BEARISH threshold. Today, new tariffs on 99.4% of US imports — a stagflationary input that arrives simultaneously with an oil shock and FOMC week — make the August CPI print nearly mathematically certain to be adverse, regardless of whether oil retreats to $95 in the next two weeks. GOOGL's -7% on $195-205B capex guidance was the first confirmation that the market is beginning to price AI infrastructure spending as a multiple-compression event, not a growth-re-rating event; META (July 29) and MSFT (July 29) report into the same investor framework with the same question unanswered. If either META or MSFT guides to 2027 capex increases — as GOOGL's CFO did — the AI capex overhang trade could erase another $500-800B in Mag 7 market cap in a single session, pushing SPX through the 7,380 BEARISH threshold. INTC's earnings blowout is the lone structural bull argument, but it is an 18-24 month revenue story; the tariff, rate, and capex headwinds are hitting cost structures in real time. Bear case trigger: SPX closes below 7,380 (formal BEARISH regime activation), OR META/MSFT guide to 2027 capex increases replicating GOOGL's -7% reaction on July 29, OR FOMC July 28-29 statement signals September hike as the base case (probability above 90%). Any one of these three triggers warrants moving from STEP ASIDE to BEARISH/DEFENSIVE.
